value.text:
Some backs have a great season. Malakai Sawyer keeps having them.

He has played 243 games and carried the ball 2,284 times for 16,436 yards, better than seven yards a carry, with 299 rushing touchdowns. He catches it too: 233 receptions for 1,852 yards and 60 more scores. Two Offensive Player of the Year awards say the league noticed.

It started in Tennessee, where he was Rookie of the Year on the Titans team that won it all in Y72. Seattle came next, then the Jets, where he won a second ring in Y77 and ran for 212 yards in a single game in Y78, still the best on the record board. Four seasons in Atlanta followed, and then the road led back to New York, where he is still carrying the ball.

Malakai Sawyer, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.tagline: A record season on the ground, a second straight title in Atlanta, and the Broncos still waiting.

articles.headline: Atlanta Does It Again
articles.dek: The Falcons went 13-3-1 and edged the Broncos 32-28 in Super Bowl CXLIII. A record season from Ryland Maxwell carried them there.
body: The Falcons are champions again. Atlanta finished the regular season 13-3-1, survived a four-point final against the Denver Broncos, 32-28 in Super Bowl CXLIII, and gave Dorren Skura a third straight title: one with the Jets, now two with the Falcons. A roster that was torn apart and rebuilt after the first ring simply did it again.

This one was won on the ground. Ryland Maxwell ran for 2,272 yards and 27 touchdowns, the best rushing season the record board has ever shown, and finished the job as Super Bowl MVP. He played all 20 games of the run and now owns 4 rings in 97 career games. A year ago he was the Offensive Player of the Year. This year he was something more.

Vyncint Heath supplied the rest. The receiver they call "Starscream" caught 119 passes for 2,209 yards and 22 touchdowns and won Offensive Player of the Year for the second time, with a card that climbed into the S tier.

The newcomers fit. Shawn Milne, who came from Tampa Bay in the trade that sent Shareef London the other way, won the first ring of his career. Chance Woodrum, one of the three champions who followed the coach south from New York, now has 5. Eric Raimann, Jashaun Fleming, Simeon Otton and Trysten Floyd each collected a second.
Up the coast, the old club had a milestone of its own. Malakai Sawyer ran for 1,551 yards and 31 touchdowns for the Jets and crossed into the Hall of Fame. He keeps running. So do the Falcons.

articles.headline: Maxwell Runs Into the Record Book
articles.dek: 2,272 rushing yards in one season, a Super Bowl MVP and a fourth ring before his hundredth game.
body: No back on the record board had ever had a season like it. Ryland Maxwell carried the Falcons for 2,272 yards in Y84, the new mark for the best rushing season, and added 27 rushing touchdowns plus 4 more as a receiver.

It was a jump even from the year he won Offensive Player of the Year, when he ran for 1,919. His career now reads 7,705 rushing yards and 102 rushing touchdowns in 97 games, 6.7 yards a carry for a career, and the season pushed him past 100 rushing scores.

The market noticed. His card rose from an overall of 67 to 75 and from a C+ grade to B+, and its value went from 20 to 112. With 4 rings and a Super Bowl MVP before his hundredth game, Maxwell has stopped being the back who followed the coach from New York. He is the reason Atlanta keeps winning.

articles.headline: Starscream, Again
articles.dek: A second Offensive Player of the Year for Vyncint Heath, and a card that reached the S tier.
body: Vyncint Heath did not need a full year to prove the first one was no accident. In 18 games he caught 119 passes for 2,209 yards and 22 touchdowns, 18.6 yards a catch, and the league handed him a second Offensive Player of the Year award.
He has now played 56 games and caught 341 passes for 6,305 yards and 64 touchdowns, more than one score a game. He also has 3 rings, two of them won since the trade that brought him to Atlanta.

The grade followed the numbers. His card went from A+ to S, its overall from 70 to 77, and its value from 29 to 124, the biggest climb on the Falcons roster. At this pace the career totals will not stay modest for long.

articles.headline: Denver Meets Skura, and Loses, Again
articles.dek: Four Super Bowls against the Broncos, four wins, with three different clubs across 68 seasons.
body: The Broncos have now reached the final against Dorren Skura four times and lost every one. The first came in Y16, a 22-16 win with the Commanders. Two more followed with the Buccaneers, 46-11 in Y23 and 38-16 in Y25. Then nothing for nearly six decades, until Atlanta beat Denver 32-28 in Super Bowl CXLIII.

This was the closest of the four by a distance. The first three were decided by six points or more, two of them by more than three touchdowns. Denver had a four-point game and a tight end who knows the Falcons well: D.C Paradis, who has 995 career catches, played all 20 games of the Broncos' run and is now five catches short of a thousand.
For Skura it is a rivalry measured in eras. The Commanders, the Buccaneers dynasty and now the Falcons have all taken their turn, and the Broncos are still waiting for their first win.

articles.headline: Sawyer Runs Into the Hall
articles.dek: Twelve seasons after his rookie title in Tennessee, Malakai Sawyer crossed the Career Legacy line, and he is still carrying the ball for the Jets.
body: Malakai Sawyer did not slow down to get there. In his second season back with the Jets he ran for 1,551 yards and 31 touchdowns in 19 games, passed 15,000 career rushing yards along the way, and finished the year with a Career Legacy of 7,101, enough for the Hall of Fame.

The totals are a career's worth: 16,436 rushing yards and 299 rushing touchdowns in 243 games, plus 233 catches for 60 more scores. He was Rookie of the Year on the Titans team that won it all in Y72, won a second ring with the Jets in Y77, and collected 2 Offensive Player of the Year awards along the way.

The market had already decided. His card's value went from 3,153 to 5,679 this season, and its overall reached 96. He was the man the Jets took back when Skura left for Atlanta, and he has made that trade look good from both sides.

articles.headline: Life After Atlanta
articles.dek: Brandon Jaclyde, Shareef London and Perrion Randall left the champions after one season. All three spent Y84 watching their old club win again.
body: The Falcons traded away three pieces of their first title team, and none of them got a second ring. Brandon Jaclyde, the reigning Most Valuable Player, went to Miami and threw for 2,807 yards and 26 touchdowns with only 2 interceptions in 17 games for the Dolphins. Solid, but a long way from the 56 touchdowns he threw as a Falcon.
Shareef London went to Tampa Bay in the deal for Shawn Milne and caught 61 passes for 464 yards and 5 scores with the Buccaneers, 7.6 yards a catch. Milne, meanwhile, collected the ring.

Perrion Randall played 17 games for the Seahawks and was credited with 16 blocks. His card actually climbed, its overall from 66 to 74, even as his grade fell from the S tier to B+. For all three, Atlanta was a single season, a single ring, and then a view from somewhere else.

articles.headline: Two Former Jets Stars Go Quiet
articles.dek: Kane Van Oxley and Jaylen Conklin piled up catches in Y84 but found almost no room to run after them.
body: Kane Van Oxley built a career on the deep ball: 16,215 yards on 968 catches, 16.8 yards every time he touched it. In his second season with the Bears he caught 60 passes for 385 yards, 6.4 a catch, with 5 touchdowns. His grade slipped from A+ to A, though collectors kept buying; the card's value still rose from 1,906 to 2,150.

Jaylen Conklin, still with the Jets, caught 85 passes for 513 yards and 5 scores, barely 6 yards a reception for a tight end who used to make the big play look routine. His card was one of the few to lose value this season, from 748 to 713.

Neither has lost his place in the league's history. Van Oxley has 160 receiving touchdowns and 3 rings. But for the first time in a while, the numbers say these two are being used to move the chains rather than to change games.

articles.headline: The Class That Arrived Ready
articles.dek: A rookie back with 31 touchdowns, a quarterback who barely missed, and an A+ grade or better for three first-year cards.
body: The new cards this season did not look like first-year cards. Angelo Moton ran for 1,717 yards and 31 touchdowns in his first 20 games, 9.3 yards a carry, and was named Rookie of the Year. His card opened with an A+ grade.

Orlando Larienne completed 205 of his 233 passes for 3,485 yards and 41 touchdowns in 15 games and already owns a ring. Jimmy Tillery threw 589 times in his first 19 games and was intercepted only 4 times, with 27 touchdown passes and 3,392 yards.

Calais Ham, an offensive lineman, made 49 blocks in 20 games, debuted in the S tier and has a ring of his own. Veterans joined the card pool too: Vic Cannon arrives with 59,531 career passing yards, and Terron Stidham with 1,980 tackles.

articles.headline: Record Watch: Settle Joins the Tackle Race
articles.dek: K'Lavon Settle passed 2,500 tackles and moved within 317 of the all-time mark.
body: The career tackle record belongs to Mose Junior at 2,862, and the chase has a new name in it. K'Lavon Settle made 189 tackles and picked off 5 passes in Y84, passed 2,500 for his career and now sits at 2,545, 317 short. Dan Mosley remains closer at 2,658, 204 away, but Settle has momentum: his card rose from an overall of 89 to 93 and from an A− grade to A+.
Settle is also climbing the interception list with 32, 8 behind Jayon Queen's 40. Mosley, at 37, is 3 away from that one.
Elsewhere, Kalif Suh has 10 forced fumbles, 1 short of Tyrone Baugh's 11. In the backfield, Derrick Myrick has 347 rushing touchdowns, 41 behind Trequan Jensen's 388.

value.tagline: One more title in green, then the coach walked out the door and the league traded everything that wasn't nailed down.

articles.headline: The Last Dance in New York
articles.dek: The Jets went 15-2, beat the Eagles in Super Bowl CXLI and handed Dorren Skura another title. Then the coach took the keys to Atlanta.
body: The Jets did what the Jets do under Dorren Skura. They finished 15-2, ran the bracket and beat the Eagles in Super Bowl CXLI. The final was 46-8. It was another Super Bowl title for the coach and New York's third in a seven-season run that also delivered CXXXVI in Y77 and CXXXIX in Y80.

The engine was Kane Van Oxley. The Ox added 145 catches, 2,496 yards and 39 touchdowns across 20 games in Y82, took the MVP and climbed into the S tier of the skill grades. Ty Lock threw for 4,909 yards and 61 touchdowns and walked off with the Super Bowl MVP. A first-year receiver, Vyncint Heath, caught 85 balls for 1,592 yards and was named Offensive Player of the Year. Up front, Jakeem Friend collected ring number 7.

Then the map changed. Before Y83 kicked off, the coach moved to the Falcons and took Van Oxley, Ryland Maxwell and Chance Woodrum with him, sending Malakai Sawyer back to the Jets. A wave of three- and four-way trades followed: Lock to the Giants, Van Oxley on to the Bears, Heath and Shareef London to Atlanta, Drake Wise through Atlanta and on to the Ravens, Dan Stout to New York.
One offseason was all it took to break up a champion. This is the story of the Y82 season, the last title of the Jets era, and the scramble that came after it.

articles.headline: Atlanta Calling, Then the Shuffle
articles.dek: The coach took three champions south and kept two. When the trades stopped, the Falcons were Heath, London, Maxwell and Woodrum, and The Ox was a Bear.
body: It started with the coach. Dorren Skura walked away from the champion Jets for the Falcons and took three of his title core with him: Kane Van Oxley, Ryland Maxwell and Chance Woodrum. Malakai Sawyer went the other way, back to New York.

That was only the opening act. Before a down of Y83, the league erupted in three- and four-way trades and Atlanta's haul changed shape. Kane Van Oxley, the reigning MVP, never played a game in red: he was flipped to the Bears. Drake Wise, brought in from the Giants for an unnamed quarterback, was a Falcon just long enough to be moved on to the Ravens. In came Vyncint Heath from the Jets and Shareef London from the Bears.

So the coach's first Falcons are Heath, London, Maxwell and Woodrum. Maxwell, 2 rings in 56 games and 1,430 rushing yards in Y82, is the back. Woodrum brings 3 rings and 931 tackles to a brand new secondary. London, 2,849 yards and 37 touchdowns in 86 games, gets a fresh start with a contender.
For Van Oxley it is pure whiplash: a title, an MVP, a ticket to Atlanta and then Chicago, all in one offseason. For Atlanta it is a reset built around the two Jets who stayed with their coach.

articles.headline: Champions Nobody Recognizes
articles.dek: The Jets kept the trophy. The coach, the MVP, the Super Bowl MVP and the Offensive Player of the Year all left. This is who is left to defend it.
body: Count what is gone from New York: Dorren Skura to Atlanta, Van Oxley to Chicago, Lock to the Giants, Heath to the Falcons, Maxwell and Woodrum with the coach. Half the roster that hung the CXLI banner has scattered.

What stays is the spine. Jakeem Friend, 7 rings and 526 blocks, still anchors the line. Jaylen Conklin, the tight end known as “Takeoff” for a vertical that lets him snatch anything thrown above his head, brings 4,502 yards and 66 touchdowns. Kalif Suh forced 4 fumbles in Y82 and sits at 10 for his career. Trequan Roberts, 2 rings, and rookie Dwayne Skura hold the secondary.

The new faces are familiar ones. Dan Stout takes over at quarterback, and Malakai Sawyer comes home: a Jet from Y76 to Y78 and a champion in Y77, he ran for 1,169 yards and 26 touchdowns for the Falcons last season and returns with 13,041 career rushing yards.
It should feel strange in New York this year. The banner is fresh, the faces are not, and Stout, ringless in 264 games, has just been handed a team that knows how to win one.

articles.headline: Three Quarterbacks, Three New Homes
articles.dek: The Super Bowl MVP is a Giant, the Ravens' starter now runs the champions' offense, and Drake Wise was a Falcon for exactly one trade.
body: Ty Lock leaves New York with 2 rings, 2 MVPs and a Super Bowl MVP from CXLI. His career line reads 22,189 yards and 239 touchdowns in 93 games, and the multi-team deals sent all of it to the Giants. Lock walks out a champion, the rare player who leaves on top.

His replacement is a volume passer still hunting a first ring. Dan Stout has thrown for 48,796 yards and 472 touchdowns in 264 games without one, and his Y82 in Baltimore added 3,055 yards, 26 touchdowns and only 4 interceptions. Now he inherits the defending champions, and with them the one thing his career has never had: a real shot at a ring.

Drake Wise took the strangest route. The coach traded an unnamed quarterback to the Giants to bring him to Atlanta, and the league-wide shuffle moved him on to the Ravens before he took a snap there. He arrives in Baltimore with 2 MVPs, 45,968 yards and 467 touchdowns, and like Stout, no ring. His Y82: 3,331 yards, 33 touchdowns, 3 interceptions.

articles.headline: The Ox and Starscream
articles.dek: Kane Van Oxley played his way into the S tier. Vyncint Heath played his way onto the map in 17 games.
body: Van Oxley's Y82 was a highlight reel in numbers: 2,496 yards on 145 catches, 17.2 a catch, with 39 touchdowns. That is a touchdown on more than a quarter of his receptions. They call him “The Ox” for the strength that breaks tackles and holds up blocks, and no player Skura has coached has recovered more fumbles. The market caught on this year: his value went from 716 to 1,515, up 111.6%. He now carries 14,921 career yards, 147 touchdowns and 3 rings to Chicago, a Falcon for a moment and a Bear for real.

Heath was the surprise. In his first 17 games he caught 85 passes for 1,592 yards, 18.7 a catch, won Offensive Player of the Year and a ring, and debuted with a skill grade of A−. They call him “Starscream”. The multi-team trades sent him to Atlanta, so he still plays for the coach who watched him break out, now beside Maxwell and Woodrum.

articles.headline: The Other Side of the Ledger
articles.dek: Not every stock went up. Two veteran receivers lost their bite and the market cooled on two defenders.
body: Juawan Lance has 4 rings and 15,422 career yards, but his Y82 season added 396 yards on 45 catches. That is 8.8 a catch for a receiver who averages 13.2 over his career. Craig Whitney caught 85 balls and turned them into just 442 yards, 5.2 a catch against a career 9.9, and his skill grade slipped to C−.

On defense, Darrel Longa logged 95 tackles in 17 games, yet his OVR dropped from 75 to 73 and his market value fell 22.5%. Taywan Tuttle's value dropped 43.5% without a new game played, the steepest fall on the market this season.
None of it erases a career. It does show which way these careers are trending.

articles.headline: Record Watch: Jensen Closes In
articles.dek: Trequan Jensen is one big season from Rondale Ikarras. The tackles race has a new name in it.
body: Ikarras holds the league's career rushing mark at 23,178 yards. Trequan Jensen sits at 21,690, 1,488 short, after a Y82 that added 1,390 yards and 19 touchdowns. One more season like that leaves him knocking on the door. He already has more career rushing touchdowns than anyone in league history, 388 to Ikarras's 374.

The tackles record belongs to Mose Junior at 2,862. Dan Mosley has 2,658 and added none in Y82, and Abraham Ward Jr has pulled to 2,653, right on his heels. Mosley also has 37 interceptions, 3 behind Jayon Queen's 40.
Kalif Suh forced 4 fumbles in Y82. That puts him at 10 for his career, one behind Tyrone Baugh's league-best 11.

articles.headline: Milestones: 50,000, 2,500 and a 7th Ring
articles.dek: Kirk Lenoir joined the 50,000-yard club, Ward Jr joined the Hall of Fame, and Jakeem Friend kept collecting jewelry.
body: Kirk Lenoir crossed 50,000 career passing yards with a Y82 that added 3,386 yards and 37 touchdowns. He now sits at 51,978, though his skill grade dipped to D+ on the way. Jason Macleone keeps climbing too: 73,799 yards, 771 touchdowns and 331 games, fourth on the career passing list.

Abraham Ward Jr passed 2,500 tackles and crossed Career Legacy 7,000, which makes him the Hall of Fame's Y82 class. The Packers defensive back has 2,653 tackles and 33 interceptions in 236 games, a Defensive Player of the Year and a ring.
Jakeem Friend won his 7th ring with the Jets and passed 500 career blocks, now 526 in 252 games. Linemen do not win MVPs. They win this.

articles.headline: Same Opponent, Different Uniform
articles.dek: Three Super Bowls against the Eagles, three wins, with three different clubs.
body: Philadelphia keeps finding Dorren Skura on the biggest stage, and it keeps ending the same way. He beat the Eagles 36-28 in CVIII with the Ravens in Y49, 38-11 in CXXXI with the Titans in Y72, and again in CXLI with the Jets. That is three meetings and three wins, each in a different uniform.

The thread runs through Malakai Sawyer. He was Rookie of the Year on that Y72 Titans team, the only season he ever spent in Tennessee, and he is the man the Jets got back when the coach left for Atlanta. If the Eagles get there again, they will meet a fourth Skura club: the Falcons.

articles.headline: Where Are They Now: The Ones Who Walked
articles.dek: Alvin Tufele retired, Dylan Hyatt left the league and Blair Iupati never played a down in green.
body: Before Y82 the Jets let two champions walk out the door, and a third never really arrived. Dylan Hyatt was not brought back and left the league. Alvin Tufele was let go too and has since retired. Blair Iupati came over from Seattle in a trade and was shipped on to New Orleans almost as soon as he landed.

Tufele came over from Seattle in the Obinna Leary trade, played Y81 for the Jets and is done: 230 games, 1,158 catches, 18,352 yards, 188 touchdowns and 3 rings. Hyatt leaves with 6 rings, 1,713 tackles and 231 games, his last club the Jets.
Iupati was a Jet for about as long as a trade call lasts. The Seahawks defensive back, 112 games and a ring, went on to the Saints before he ever suited up in New York.

value.tagline: A new club, a new quarterback, a new receiver in full flight, and the old champions waiting in the final.

articles.headline: Year One in Atlanta Ends With a Ring
articles.dek: The Falcons went 12-5, ran the table in the playoffs and beat the Jets 40-25 in Super Bowl CXLII. Dorren Skura's first season in red ended against the club he left.
body: Nobody gave the Falcons a bye. They finished 12-5, played their way in through the first weekend of the playoffs and did not lose again, finishing 40-25 over the New York Jets in Super Bowl CXLII. It was another title for Dorren Skura, won in his first season with a new club, against the champions he had coached a year earlier.

The offense belonged to people who were not in Atlanta a year before. Brandon Jaclyde, in his first 21 games in the league, threw for 5,199 yards and 56 touchdowns and was named Most Valuable Player. Vyncint Heath, the receiver they call "Starscream", turned a trade into the best season of his young career: 137 catches, 2,504 yards, 34 touchdowns and the Super Bowl MVP. Ryland Maxwell ran for 1,919 yards and 25 scores and won Offensive Player of the Year.

The defense was new too. Simeon Otton was Rookie of the Year at linebacker, Jashaun Fleming worked the line, and Trysten Floyd joined Chance Woodrum in the secondary. Woodrum, one of the three champions who followed the coach south, now owns 4 rings.
On the other sideline stood the club Skura built. Malakai Sawyer and Jaylen Conklin carried the Jets back to the final, and lost to Skura on Super Bowl Sunday for the third time in three meetings.

The celebration did not last long. Before the second season in Atlanta began, Shareef London went to Tampa Bay for Shawn Milne, Jaclyde was traded to the Dolphins and Perrion Randall to the Seahawks. The champions are already a different team.

articles.headline: Jaclyde: One Season, One MVP, One Ring, One Trade
articles.dek: Brandon Jaclyde threw 56 touchdown passes in his first 21 games, won the MVP and the Super Bowl, and was a Dolphin before his second season began.
body: A year ago the quarterback question in Atlanta was a revolving door. Drake Wise came and went in a single trade, and the Falcons opened Y83 with a passer who had never taken a snap in the league. Brandon Jaclyde answered it emphatically.

In 21 games he threw for 5,199 yards and 56 touchdowns, about two and a half scores a game, and took the league's Most Valuable Player award. His 26 interceptions say he never stopped taking shots, and with Heath running past people, most of those shots landed. He also ran it in 4 times.
The skill grades rate him in the A band already. The market is slower: his card opened at a value of 19, a long way below the established passers he outplayed.

Then the business side arrived. Before the Falcons' second season, Jaclyde was traded to the Dolphins. Miami gets a reigning MVP with one season on his card, and Atlanta goes looking for its third starting quarterback in three offseasons.

articles.headline: Starscream Takes Flight
articles.dek: Vyncint Heath caught 137 passes for 2,504 yards and 34 touchdowns, then took the Super Bowl MVP. His skill grade climbed to A+.
body: Last season "Starscream" was a promising rookie with 85 catches on a loaded Jets roster. This season he was the reason defensive coordinators lost sleep.

Heath played all 21 Falcons games and caught 137 passes for 2,504 yards and 34 touchdowns. That is 18.3 yards a catch on a season's worth of volume, and a touchdown on roughly one of every four receptions. When the Falcons needed one more play in Super Bowl CXLII, it went his way, and so did the game's MVP award.

Two seasons in, he has 2 rings, an Offensive Player of the Year award and a Super Bowl MVP. The skill grades moved him from A- to A+, and his card value jumped 262 percent. The ceiling is not in sight yet.

articles.headline: Maxwell Carries the Load, and the Hardware
articles.dek: Ryland Maxwell ran for 1,919 yards and 25 touchdowns, won Offensive Player of the Year and added a third ring.
body: Ryland Maxwell was one of the three champions who followed Skura out of New York, and he made the move look like a promotion. In Atlanta he was the every-down back: 1,919 rushing yards and 25 rushing touchdowns across 21 games, plus another 10 catches out of the backfield.
The league noticed. Maxwell was named Offensive Player of the Year, the first individual award of his career beyond his Rookie of the Year trophy, and the Super Bowl win gave him 3 rings in 77 games.

The market has been slower to catch up. His skill grade sits at C+ and his card value of 20 is modest for a back with his resume, which makes him one of the better bargains on the board heading into the second Atlanta season, where he remains on the roster.

articles.headline: The Rest of the Roster Nobody Knew
articles.dek: A rookie of the year at linebacker, an S-grade lineman and a tight end who scored on almost a quarter of his catches.
body: Champions are remembered by their stars, but this Falcons team was built out of first-year cards. Eric Raimann caught 54 passes for 792 yards and 13 touchdowns at tight end. Perrion Randall was credited with 58 blocks in 21 games on the line and debuted with a skill score of 99, the top of the S tier.

On defense, Simeon Otton made 94 tackles at linebacker and was named Rookie of the Year. Jashaun Fleming matched him with 94 tackles and added 3 sacks up front. Trysten Floyd made 62 tackles, picked off a pass and forced a fumble in a secondary anchored by Chance Woodrum, who added 117 tackles and a fourth ring.
Every one of them now has a ring in his first season. Not all of them will wear red in the next one: Randall was traded to the Seahawks before the second Atlanta season.

articles.headline: Beating the Team He Built
articles.dek: The defending champion Jets made it back to the Super Bowl with Skura's old core. Skura is now 3-0 against New York on Super Bowl Sunday.
body: The Jets did not collapse after the coach left. With Dan Stout running the offense, Malakai Sawyer back in green and Jaylen Conklin still catching everything thrown above his head, New York returned to the final. Sawyer ran for 1,844 yards and 37 touchdowns, Conklin added 122 catches for 908 yards and 9 scores, and Kalif Suh made 54 more tackles.
It was not enough. The Falcons won 40-25, and Skura moved to 3-0 in Super Bowls against the Jets, with three different clubs.

The market still rated the losers' season. Conklin's card value rose 313 percent, the biggest jump in the league, even as his skill grade slipped from A+ to A. Sawyer's grade rose to B+ and his card value climbed 80 percent. Suh's card value tripled. The roster that won CXLI is still good enough to win another; it simply ran into the coach who assembled it.

articles.headline: Champions, Then Sellers
articles.dek: Shareef London went to Tampa Bay for Shawn Milne, Jaclyde to Miami and Randall to Seattle before the second Atlanta season.
body: Shareef London's Atlanta chapter lasted one season. He arrived from the Bears in the Y83 multi-team trades, caught 91 passes for 1,579 yards, won the first ring of his career, and was then shipped to the Buccaneers for Shawn Milne before the second Falcons season. London leaves with 45 career touchdowns and a card value that rose 50 percent in his year as a Falcon.

He was not the only champion out the door. The MVP, Brandon Jaclyde, was traded to the Dolphins. Perrion Randall, an S-grade lineman after one season, was traded to the Seahawks, the club Skura's Jets beat in Super Bowls CXXXVI and CXXXIX.

What remains in Atlanta is the spine: Heath, Maxwell, Woodrum and the young defense of Otton, Fleming and Floyd, with Raimann at tight end. The coach has rebuilt on the fly before. He will have to do it again in year two.

articles.headline: Where the Old Jets Landed
articles.dek: Ty Lock found his footing with the Giants, Drake Wise posted 38 touchdowns in Baltimore and The Ox spent his first season as a Bear outside the playoffs.
body: Last offseason's trades scattered the Jets' stars around the league. One season later, the returns are in.

Ty Lock played 19 games for the Giants, a playoff appearance included, and threw for 3,678 yards and 33 touchdowns. The skill grades cooled on him slightly, from A+ to A-. Drake Wise, who passed through Atlanta on paper only, threw for 3,496 yards and 38 touchdowns for the Ravens in 19 games, and his card value rose 33 percent.

Kane Van Oxley had the quietest year of the three. "The Ox" played 17 games for the Bears with no postseason, catching 58 passes for 909 yards and 8 touchdowns. His skill grade slipped out of the S tier to A+.

articles.headline: Record Watch: The Jensen Chase Ends Short
articles.dek: Trequan Jensen retired after Y83 with the rushing record still in Rondale Ikarras's hands. The tackles chase belongs to Dan Mosley, with K'Lavon Settle coming.
body: For two seasons the question was whether Trequan Jensen had one more big year in him. He played Y83 and then retired, and the career rushing record still belongs to Rondale Ikarras. Through Y82, Jensen had 21,690 rushing yards, 1,488 short of the mark; his final season's line was never recorded, but the record did not change hands.
That leaves the tackles chase as the league's headline pursuit. Dan Mosley's latest card holds 2,658 tackles, 204 behind Mose Junior's record.

The name to watch behind him is K'Lavon Settle. He added 238 tackles in 17 games, climbed to 2,356 for his career and moved up to an 89 overall with an A- grade. At that pace the tackles leaderboard will have a new name near the top within a few seasons.

articles.headline: Market Report: Winners, and Two Backs in Free Fall
articles.dek: Conklin, Iupati and Tim Wright more than tripled their card values. JR Bashaam and Tramon Amerson lost nearly half of theirs.
body: The card market rewarded production this season. Jaylen Conklin's value rose 313 percent, Blair Iupati's 300 percent after 474 tackles in 34 games since his last card, and Tim Wright's 283 percent on the back of 2,871 rushing yards and 64 touchdowns across 37 games.

The other side of the ledger belonged to two running backs who did not get a new card. JR Bashaam's value fell 46 percent as his OVR slid from 69 to 65, and Tramon Amerson's fell 42 percent with a drop from 71 to 68. Jake Gano, a defensive lineman, lost 22 percent.
The lesson of the market is the lesson of the league: the cards that move are the ones that keep playing.

articles.headline: Three Veterans Walk Away
articles.dek: Dan Stout, Jakeem Friend and Trequan Jensen all played Y83 and retired when it ended.
body: The offseason after the Falcons' title took three long careers with it.

Dan Stout quarterbacked the Jets in his one season in New York, all the way to Super Bowl CXLII, after a long career in Baltimore. He retires without a ring. Through Y82 he had thrown for 48,796 yards and 472 touchdowns against just 51 interceptions.

Jakeem Friend walks away a seven-time champion on the offensive line. He had 7 rings and 526 blocks across 252 games through Y82, most of those seasons spent in Seattle, and he finished his career in green.
Trequan Jensen retires a Packer, with 21,690 rushing yards and 388 rushing touchdowns through Y82 and the Y79 title on his resume.
Their final Y83 lines were never recorded, so the careers above stand as the books through Y82.
